title: plugin-calendar: authoring `currentDate` as the ISO string its own registry input documents crashes calendar-view
body:
Measured while fixing #4433, in the same renderer, but a different key and a different mechanism — a missing string→Date conversion, not a prop collision. Not fixed there: out of that card's scope.

## The defect

`packages/plugin-calendar/src/calendar-view-renderer.tsx` declares the input:

```
{ name: 'currentDate', type: 'string', label: 'Current Date',
  description: 'ISO date string for initial calendar date' }
```

`CalendarViewProps.currentDate` is a **`Date`**. The renderer never converts: the authored value reaches `CalendarView` through the trailing `{...props}` spread exactly as written, becomes `useState`'s initial `selectedDate`, and the header calls `selectedDate.toLocaleDateString(…)` on a string.

## Measured, in isolation

Node authored per the input's own description:

```json
{ "type": "plugin-calendar:calendar-view", "id": "n",
  "data": [ ... ],
  "currentDate": "2026-08-12T08:00:00.000Z" }
```

renders the error boundary, not the calendar:

```
Component "plugin-calendar:calendar-view" failed to render
selectedDate.toLocaleDateString is not a function
```

The same node without `currentDate` renders the real calendar (`role="region" aria-label="Calendar"`). Measured again after #4433's fix landed — unchanged, so the two defects are independent.

## Why it is worth its own card

This is the reverse of #4433's shape. There, an authored key that no one documents took the component down. Here the component **documents the key, documents its type, and documents the format**, and honouring that documentation is what breaks it — the one spelling an author is told to use is the one that cannot work. There is no correct authored value: the registry says `type: 'string'` and the component takes a `Date`, so a metadata author cannot express the working form at all.

Related surface, not the same bug: #4433 (the `events` collision, fixed) is about the spread OVERWRITING a computed prop; this is about a declared input never being converted before it reaches the spread.
